boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Fisher's Hill record (September 21-22, 1864) in Sheridan's Valley Campaign [August-October 1864]. The September 20 advance to Strasburg, Torbert's Luray Valley operations and the September 23-25 pursuit are context. Campaign-wide marches, destruction, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 38,944 total (US 29,444; CS 9,500); the live field reads 48450 (US 38950; CS 9500). Early says his line at Fisher's Hill was very thin, and on September 25 put the enemy at three or four to one. Pond says Early occupied the position when he no longer had men enough to cover it, with a force too broken and dispirited to hold it.
claims.rationale: The frozen and live Union figures differ by 9,506 and no source basis is given; Early's ratio is an interested estimate. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: Pond says the Valley narrows here to four miles between the Massanutten and North Mountain, that Fisher's Hill is a precipitous bluff over Tumbling Run, and that the ground before it was densely wooded and broken by ledges and ravines. Early says the position could be flanked, like every position in the Valley.
claims.rationale: Ground described by a history and an interested report. Pond says Early's line was substantially the one he had held in August and that he began erecting additional works on arriving; the claim stays unresolved. No map verification.

The frozen commanders are Lieutenant General Early and Major General Sheridan; the live page gives Early as Major General.
claims.rationale: Command roles from a history and an interested report; neither listed commander receives automatic sole credit, and the live rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty fields read 1,763 total (US 528; CS 1,235). Early gives his infantry and artillery loss as 30 killed, 210 wounded and 995 missing, total 1,235, says the enemy captured no more than 400 or 500, and that twelve guns were lost; Pond says sixteen guns were captured, that Sheridan reported 1,100 prisoners, and puts Sheridan's loss at about 400 and Early's at 1,300 to 1,400.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Sheridan's 1866 report passage on the battle (read, not selected), his September 20-25 dispatches, Crook's, Wright's, Ricketts's and Torbert's reports, Lomax's report, the compiled Union return (No. 5) and Hotchkiss's journal remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. George E. Pond's The Shenandoah Valley in 1864 (Scribner, 1883) is a retrospective history written, by its preface, from the official documents at the War Records Office and field despatches; it quotes Sheridan's, Torbert's, Wright's and Early's reports and despatches and is not independent of them. Early's reports and dispatches of September 23-October 21, 1864 to Lee are one family of interested Confederate accounts; it is the same author family as his July 14 report selected for Early's Raid. Official Records Series I, Volume XLIII, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
